title: Nonclosed points in finite-type schemes have infinitely many closed specializations
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $z\in X$ is not closed, then the closure $\overline{\{z\}}$ contains infinitely many closed points of $X$ [def-weil-closed-points].

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), together with Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), which gives positive dimension for the closure of a nonclosed point and hence infinitely many closed specializations

proof.text: By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], X is Jacobson. Thus, for Z = closure {z}, the closed points of X in Z have closure Z. In Lean this is LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace f followed by closure_inter_closedPoints isClosed_closure.

Suppose S = Z ∩ closedPoints X is finite. Express S as the finite union of its closed singleton subsets. Then S is closed (Set.Finite.isClosed_biUnion), so its closure is S. The preceding equality gives S = Z. Since z belongs to Z, z belongs to closedPoints X, contradicting the assumption that {z} is not closed. Hence S is infinite. This uses only the definition of closed points, finite unions of closed sets, and the Jacobson equality from step 1.
